This is a well-structured, accessible HTML5 document demonstrating modern best practices for semantic markup and inclusive design.

It uses semantic landmarks, a skip link for keyboard navigation, and CSS that adapts to your light or dark mode preference.

Text and link colors meet WCAG AA contrast in both themes, type scales with your browser's font size, and motion respects your system settings.

Features

  • Semantic HTML structure with proper landmarks
  • Keyboard accessible navigation and focus management
  • Dark mode support with custom color schemes
  • Responsive typography using modern CSS
  • Print-friendly styles for better readability
  • WCAG AA contrast compliance in all color modes

Examples

Component Cards

Card components are useful for organizing related content. They include a subtle border and padding for visual separation.

Learn more about accessibility resources

Interactive Elements

Buttons and links are fully accessible with clear focus states. All interactive elements include visible focus indicators and proper ARIA labels.

Keyboard navigation: Use Tab to move forward, Shift+Tab to move backward, and Enter or Space to activate.

Perfect! I've successfully improved the HTML document. Here's a summary of the enhancements made:

## Key Improvements:

**1. Semantic Structure**
- Added a proper `<h2>` heading to the introduction section instead of relying only on `aria-label`
- Improved heading hierarchy throughout the document

**2. Form Enhancements**
- Wrapped form fields in a `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>` for better semantic grouping
- Added error state styling (`#form-status[data-state="error"]`)
- Changed form status to use `aria-live="assertive"` for more immediate announcements
- Updated error messages to be more descriptive (e.g., "Email address is required" vs generic messages)
- Improved form feedback with visual error state indicator

**3. Accessibility Improvements**
- Increased focus outline width from 2px to 3px for better visibility
- Added extra focus visibility styling for forced-colors mode (high contrast)
- Enhanced skip link focus styling with additional visual feedback (inset box-shadow)
- Improved message counter description with separate span for "remaining" text

**4. User Experience**
- Better form error messaging that explains what needs to be corrected
- Improved success message: "Success! Thanks for your message..."
- Form now shows error state when validation fails, giving users clearer feedback

The document now has better semantic HTML structure, more accessible form handling, and improved visual feedback for keyboard navigation and form interactions. All changes maintain the existing design aesthetics while enhancing accessibility and usability.
